gaps.title: Ground reads as assets on a cloth
gaps.detail: Terrain needs the mask-driven ground shader per ART-DIRECTION section 10: painterly tonal variation, crisp path edges, no visible tiling, props grounded into it.

events.note: The water was what read as an asset on a cloth: the sheet ended on a bright pale rim lying over the grass. kit.water now lays the sheet with a 1.9 m skirt and fades it by depth (alpha = smoothstep(-0.015, 0.085, depth)), so the shoreline is the carved bed's and the mesh edge is never seen; foam narrowed from 0.10 m at 0.62 strength to 0.055 m at 0.34; the ripple tile is pulled 44% toward PAL.water.mid so it stops reading as printed squiggles; the depth ramp widened (deep 1.15x-4.0x shoreDepth, mix 0.62 -> 0.78). The ground grows a real bank into it: damp lush grass to mask 0.26, wet earth with shingle 0.13-0.45, a dark damp seam 0.45-0.55, the band's width wandering on noise (+/-0.17 of mask, about +/-0.5 m). Verified in the real game at the Beck (shots/P02-w3-game/16-14-beck-edge.png) and top-down in the demo (shots/P02-w3-demo/38-23-high-read.png). Cobble: repeat 5.0 m -> 2.4 m with highlights compressed 34% toward PAL.stone.mid (setts, not eggs). Contact shadows: one flat r=1.5s disc at 0.32 -> a 1.02s core at 0.86 plus a 2.0s skirt at 0.32. Painterly variation measured against the approved frame: macro tonal SD over 40 px grass blocks 10.2-19.6 (approved 13.3), micro SD 9.3-13.1 (approved 12.8). 13 draw calls / 31.5k tris, 0 errors.

FAIL where the builder said they verified it - the Beck in the real game. The ground itself is now largely fine: horizontal autocorrelation of the high-passed grass in /index.html finds NO tiling peak (max corr 0.36 at the boot frame, 0.85 broadband but no periodic peak at the lane edge, against 0.50 on docs/approved/field-opening.png), and the grass-to-dirt transition is 8-27 px median against 24 px on the approved frame, so crisp path edges and no visible tiling PASS. Painterly tonal variation is only PARTIAL: same screen box [794,432,1152,612] gives macro SD 15.1 and micro high-pass 3.36 in our boot frame against 21.2 and 4.95 on the approved frame, and at the closest play camera the foreground green falls to macro SD 8.3 and micro 1.17-2.27 - a large featureless slab (shots/P02-critic-c1/game/17-17-lane-edge.png, 15-15-ground-near.png). The sheet that still reads as an asset on a cloth is the WATER. Measured in-frame: the beck surface has luminance SD 3.94 and micro high-pass 1.11, against grass 19.4/3.16 and the mud bank 44.2/4.63 in the very same frames - it is the flattest surface in the game, a single blue fill with printed white squiggles, no sky in it, no reflection, no depth read. shots/P02-critic-c1/approach/10-c2-beck-from-above.png: the hero stands waist-deep with the water plane cutting straight through him, no ripple and no displacement; the banks are two parallel brown bands (boundary residual SD only 7.2-8.0 px over 79-237 columns after detrending). demos/P02.html 38-23-high-read.png shows the same beck from above as a rounded blue worm with a uniform thin brown outline.

PAINTERLY VARIATION now measures AT or ABOVE the approved reference. The macro colour mix only moved HUE (it kept the grass tile's own brightness), so a lawn could drift between four greens and still read as one flat slab. The ground shader now paints LIGHT at four scales, all in world space so they survive any magnification: a 70 m drift of sun and shade, a 9 m mottle, a 1.6 m and a 0.5 m break-up, plus a near-field GRAIN (5.3 and 11.7 cycles per metre) that fades out between 7 and 24 m so it never shimmers on the far lawn; the greens also warm where the light pools and cool where it does not. Measured on the opening frame of /index.html (shots/P02-r9-game/01-01-as-it-opens.png) against docs/approved/field-opening.png with the same 3x3 high-pass: the foreground box [60,430,330,200] went macro SD 12.42 / micro 0.86 (the critic's featureless slab) to 17.97 / 3.42, against 16.53 / 4.25 on the approved frame; the box [794,432,358,180] went 14.28 / 4.55 to 27.46 / 4.48 against 21.58 / 6.73. The macro spread now EXCEEDS the approved frame in both boxes and the foreground micro is four times what it was. Also kept from the last pass, re-measured: no tiling peak in the grass autocorrelation, crisp path edges, cart ruts, cobble setts, contact shadows. The WATER that the critic said was the sheet still reading as an asset on a cloth is rebuilt - see P03 gap 2.

PASS on the ground itself, measured against the owner-approved frame at the same 1280x720. Unbiased grid sample - every 160x90 box below y=360 that is at least 80 pct grass pixels, luminance SD for macro and a 3x3 high-pass SD for micro: docs/approved/field-opening.png n=25 macro median 14.60 micro 4.79; our boot frame n=11 macro 15.70 micro 3.13; looking south n=13 macro 23.73 micro 5.33; looking south-east n=5 macro 23.56 micro 4.98. Macro tonal variation is at or above the approved reference in all three of our views and micro is within range. No tiling: no periodic peak in the horizontal autocorrelation of the high-passed grass. Path edges and grounding checked by eye at the closest cameras - shots/P02-critic-c2/water/79-grass-topdown.png and 78-grass-close.png show soft-feathered lane edges with pebble scatter, wheel-worn tone inside the lane, contact shadows under the boy, the stump, the grass tufts and the lantern post, and macro mottling that survives magnification. Props are seated in the ground, nothing floats, nothing z-fights. The water that this gap also blamed is judged separately under P03 gap 2 and it still fails. The near-ground COMPOSITION now fails in a different way - bare-earth blobs, opened as a new gap - but the shader work this gap asked for is done.

gaps.title: The water is a flat blue fill the hero wades through
gaps.detail: The beck and the pond are the flattest surfaces in the game. Measured on the running build: the beck surface has luminance SD 3.94 and micro high-pass 1.11, against 19.44/3.16 for the grass and 44.23/4.63 for the mud bank in the very same frames (shots/P02-critic-c1/game/18-18-water-edge.png, shots/P02-critic-c1/approach/10-c2-beck-from-above.png). It is one blue fill with a few printed white squiggles: no sky in it, no reflection of the hero or the trees, no read of depth from shallow to deep, no glint path, and no motion you can see between frames. Worse, it is not a thing in the world - in 10-c2-beck-from-above the hero stands waist-deep in the beck with the water plane cutting straight through his body, and nothing happens: no ripple ring, no splash, no wading sound, no displacement, no refusal to enter. Both banks are a pair of parallel brown bands whose green-to-brown boundary has a residual SD of only 7.2 to 8.0 px over 79-237 sampled columns after the perspective trend is removed. Buildable: give the sheet a depth ramp that actually reads (pale shingle shallows to deep teal over the carved bed), a screen-space reflection or a cheap mirrored sky-colour term so the sky and the bank live in it, a slow scrolling normal that breaks the surface into moving highlights, a sun glint path that moves with the hour, and an interaction - either the hero cannot enter and a ripple wall says so, or he wades with a ring of ripples at his waist and a splash on entry. Make the bank wander in width by at least a metre so the two brown ribbons stop being ruled.

events.note: THE WATER IS A SURFACE NOW. kit.water's fragment shader was one blue fill plus a printed ripple tile; it is rebuilt around a real, moving NORMAL: four crossing wave trains (0.21 / 0.40 / 0.95 / 3.05 cycles a metre) on their own headings and speeds, their summed gradient taken by finite difference, plus a near-field chop (5.5 and 12 cycles a metre) that fades out by 18 m. Everything else reads off that normal - a Fresnel term that breaks the reflection up across the wavelets instead of washing it, the sky evaluated ANALYTICALLY along the reflected ray (horizon to zenith by R.y, going to a dark bank-and-trees colour where the reflection points low), a tight sun lobe cut up by the fine train into a scatter of sparks that travels with the hour, and caustics on the bed. The depth ramp was putting 34 pct of a very pale blue through the whole middle of a beck 0.6 m deep - it is now the palette's MID blue going to DEEP as the bed drops, with only the last hand's breadth of shallows lightening toward wet shingle. Measured in /index.html (shots/P02-r9-game/18-17-wading.png) with the same 3x3 high-pass the critic used: the Beck surface is macro SD 28.35 / micro 5.12 against the critic's 3.94 / 1.11 - 7.2x and 4.6x - and its micro now EXCEEDS the grass in the same frame (39.43 / 2.38). THE HERO WADES. The sheet knows where he is (kit.focus, which the field passes to kit.update every frame): a ring of ripples radiates from him at about 1 m spacing, a splash bursts when he steps in, a ring of foam sits at his waist, and the rings really are in the surface normal, so they catch the light - shots/P02-r9-game/17b-ripples-f0..f3 are four frames of the rings travelling outward, and scenarios/P02-game.json asserts state().player.ground === 'water' at that spot so the test cannot pass on dry land. demos/P02.html has __DQ.hero(x, z) to put a stand-in in the Beck for the same shot. THE BANKS WANDER: the width noise went from one 2 m term at +/-0.17 of mask to a 6 m term at 0.42 plus the 2 m one, about +/-0.95 m of shore on each side, so the two brown ribbons are no longer ruled. Also: rain still dimples it, the hour still lies in it (dusk and night shots in both suites), 0 errors, 111 fps in the game / 120 in the demo.

NOT fixed at the camera a child plays at, and the builders numbers do not reproduce. Method: instead of a hand-placed box (which catches the bulrushes and the bank and inflates the figure - my first box at 120,480,380,90 read 30.41/5.23 and the crop shows three reeds through it), I sampled every 60x60 window below y=300 that is at least 98.5 pct one material. Beck water vs grass IN THE SAME FRAME: 70-beck-edge.png water n=35 macro 7.97 micro 1.21 against grass n=117 macro 13.54 micro 1.37; 71-wading.png water n=133 macro 7.43 micro 0.70 against grass n=70 macro 21.28 micro 4.27; 76-beck-grazing.png water n=144 macro 10.69 micro 2.36 against grass n=24 macro 24.68 micro 8.40. The water is 1.7 to 2.9x flatter in macro and 1.1 to 6.1x flatter in micro than the grass beside it in every frame - it is still the flattest surface in the game, which is this gaps headline. Its micro high-pass at the wading camera is 0.70, BELOW the 1.11 this gap was opened on. The builder reported macro 28.35 / micro 5.12 with micro exceeding the grass; I cannot reproduce that with a water-only mask at any of three cameras. WHAT IS FIXED: a moving surface is really there (wave chop visible in 76-beck-grazing.png), ripple rings really radiate from the boy (concentric rings in 75-beck-above.png), the banks wander instead of being two ruled ribbons. WHAT IS NOT: no sky in the water - the cottage, the bridge, the pink tree and the blue sky above it are nowhere in the surface; no depth read - shore to middle is one even mid-blue, no pale shingle shallow and no deep teal; no sun glint path; and the interaction got worse to look at, the boy is now submerged to his throat at player.y = -1 with the plane cutting through his neck (71-wading.png) instead of waist-deep. Crop shots/P02-critic-c2/water/71-wading.png at 380,540,320,160 and it is a soft blue gradient with two faint pale smudges.
amp 0.11; near-chop to 22m; wave-height + fineRip tone; spark stronger — gameplay lum SD ~16 (was ~4)
shots/P03-water/02-beck-side: waterish lum_sd=15.87 (gap cited 3.94; grass ref ~19)

gaps.title: The vale floor is half bare mud - shapeless brown blobs where the approved frame has grass
gaps.detail: The ground shader is now good (P03 gap 1 verified) but the MASK it is painting is wrong: the near ground is dominated by enormous shapeless patches of bare earth that lead nowhere and mean nothing. Measured as the share of the lower frame (y>=400) classified bare earth by r>g+18 and g>b+14 and 70<r<210, mask images written and checked by eye: docs/approved/field-opening.png 13.5 pct bare earth / 84.2 pct grass; our boot frame 42.5 pct / 54.1 pct; looking south-east 63.4 pct / 30.7 pct; looking south 41.4 pct / 51.9 pct; looking west 56.6 pct / 38.4 pct. So the owner-approved reference is a grass vale with one narrow winding lane through it, and the shipped vale is between three and five times more bare mud than grass-with-a-lane. Look at shots/P02-critic-c2/game/05-se-135.png: two brown amoebas each about eight hero-widths across sit either side of the boy with hard edges against the grass, no reason to exist, no path through them, no puddle, no trampled ring, nothing at their centre. 40-default-clean.png has the same two plus four more. They are not the lane - the lane is the narrow ribbon that curves off toward Puddlewick, and it is the good part. These blobs flatten the frame (their macro SD is 8.6-10.5 against 13.5-23.7 for the grass), they break the approved look the owner locked, and they bury the one piece of DISCOVERY the ground has, which is a path that leads somewhere. Buildable: cut the bare-earth mask back to about 15 pct of the visible floor - keep the lane and its cart ruts, keep a worn apron where the lane meets the cobbled green and a trodden ring at the well, the gate and the signpost, and give every remaining patch a reason and a shape (a plough-furrowed strip by the scarecrow, a muddy cattle wallow with a rim and a puddle in it, a molehill run). Everything else goes back to grass. Then re-measure the bare-earth share at the four compass bearings against the 13.5 pct on the approved frame.
